name: Basilica -- nave, aisles and barrel vaults
_about:
A cathedral the way one is actually composed, rather than a massing of boxes: two ARCADES of piers and arches carry the nave walls; the aisles either side are roofed with their own barrel vaults; the nave is roofed with a barrel twice their span, springing well clear of the arcade's crowns; a clerestory stands between the arcade and that springing line and lets the light in over the aisle roofs. The west front carries the portal and the rose between two towers; the east end closes with a wall of three lancets.
EVERY HEIGHT IS A CONSEQUENCE. The arcade springs at 9m and its round heads crown at 12m; the clerestory stands from there to 22m, which is where the nave vault springs, and its crown is 29m. The aisle vault springs at 9m -- the arcade's own springing -- and its extrados at 13m is below the clerestory's sills, so the roof of the aisle does not cross a window. Change naveW and the nave's crown follows it, because a round barrel's rise IS half its span.
WHAT IS DRAWN is the masonry: walls with their openings and vaults with their haunches, each one solid, closed and welded. There is no roof over the vaults yet, and no transept.

params._naveW: between the inner faces of the two arcades: a round vault over it rises naveW / 2
params._pierT: the arcade wall's thickness -- the depth of a pier
params._crown: a round head rises half its span, so the arcade's arches crown here -- what everything above must clear
params._clearH: the top of the clerestory, and the line the nave vault springs from
params._bodyW: the whole body across: nave, both arcades, both aisles and their outer walls
params._arch: the profile EVERY opening is drawn with: semicircular for a Roman basilica, pointed for a Gothic one -- one word changes the whole building
params._zc: where the body's middle lies along its own axis: the village stands a cathedral's nave behind its towers, so the components have to follow it
params._spread: how far a pointed head's two centres stand apart, in half-widths: 1 is the equilateral arch, less is a drop arch, 0 is the semicircle. It is how an arch is fitted to a height.
params._arcadeH: the arcade wall runs up to the aisle's roof line: its arches crown at 12, the aisle's vault rides from there to 16.6, and the clerestory stands over that
params._along: a bay is rarely square, and a groin vault's crown is set by its LONGER arch: the arch along the nave is fitted to the height the vault has, flattening to a segmental one where a pointed head would not fit
params._aisleBays: how many bays of aisle vault, from the east: a cathedral whose west towers stand over its aisles' last bays leaves those to the towers
params._halfB: where the arcade and aisle walls are placed: a wall's thickness lies behind its line (toward the nave, turned a quarter), so the arcade's line is its OUTER face, and the aisle wall's is halfA + aisleT / 2

clerestory._about: the clerestory wall, up to the vault's top: it closes the lunette under every wall arch, which would otherwise stand open to the sky

nave vault._about: one bay of the nave's vault: two barrels crossing, so it meets the arcade along the arcade's own arch and the wall of the bay along the transverse one

west front._about: the portal and the aisle windows. The ROSE is a part of its own, stacked on this one: a wall face is cut into vertical strips, so two openings cannot share the same span of wall -- and a rose sits squarely over its portal. Standing it on the front as a separate course is how the building is built anyway.

nave ribs._about: the nave's RIB VAULT: diagonal ribs along each bay's groins and transverse ribs on its arches, laid on the vault
